symlink.text: Create a symbolic link `~/log` that points to the directory `/var/log`.

relative.text: Stand in your home directory and create the link `{{fruits}}` that points to `{{documents}}/{{fruits}}` – with a relative path.
relative.hint: `cd ~` and then `ln -s {{documents}}/{{fruits}} {{fruits}}`. A relative path in a link counts from the directory the link is in.

readlink.text: Show where the link `~/{{fruits}}` points with `readlink`.

hardlink.text: Give `~/{{notes}}` one more name: a **hard** link called `~/{{todo}}`.
hardlink.hint: `ln` without `-s`: `ln ~/{{notes}} ~/{{todo}}`. With `ls -li` you can see that both have the same inode number.

stat.text: Find out the permissions of `/etc/shadow` as digits with `stat`.
stat.hint: `stat /etc/shadow` and look at the line `Access: (0640/...)` – or just `stat -c %a /etc/shadow`.

umask.text: Change the umask so that new files can only be read and written by you, and then create the empty file `~/{{privateFile}}`.
umask.hint: `umask 077` removes every permission for the group and others. Then create the file with `touch ~/{{privateFile}}` – it gets `rw-------`.

umask-back.text: Set the umask back to the usual value `022`.
